title: Capacity audits
text: source file needs one column CCLD license numbers , want compare local values, one column local capacity value. Representative output:
code: library(ccldr) library(dplyr) library(readr)  sites <- read_csv("rr_sites_2026.csv", col_types = cols(.default = "c")) |>   mutate(local_capacity = as.integer(local_capacity)) #> # A tibble: 3 x 3 #>   site_name                 license_number local_capacity #>   <chr>                     <chr>                   <int> #> 1 Johnson Family Child Care 13423996                   14 #> 2 Agape Learning Center     013423056                  60 #> 3 Unknown Site              99999999                   24

title: Capacity audits
text: Run ccld_verify() first. screens unknown invalid licenses returns licensed capacity every facility found API. Representative output: capacity parsed CCLD CAPACITY field. license unknown, invalid, found, capacity NA.
code: verified <- ccld_verify(sites$license_number)  sites_verified <- sites |>   bind_cols(verified |> select(-input))  sites_verified |>   count(found, status, sort = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 3 x 3 #>   found status                         n #>   <lgl> <chr>                      <int> #> 1 TRUE  Licensed                     184 #> 2 TRUE  Closed, Licensee Initiated     6 #> 3 FALSE <NA>                           3

title: Capacity audits
text: Compare local capacity value current CCLD value. Keep missing values visible can reviewed instead silently dropping . Representative output:
code: capacity_audit <- sites_verified |>   mutate(     capacity_delta = capacity - local_capacity,     capacity_matches = !is.na(capacity) &       !is.na(local_capacity) &       capacity == local_capacity,     needs_capacity_review = !found |       is.na(capacity) |       is.na(local_capacity) |       capacity != local_capacity   ) #> # A tibble: 3 x 6 #>   site_name                 local_capacity capacity capacity_delta capacity_matches needs_capacity_review #>   <chr>                              <int>    <int>          <int> <lgl>            <lgl> #> 1 Johnson Family Child Care             14       14              0 TRUE             FALSE #> 2 Agape Learning Center                 54       60              6 FALSE            TRUE #> 3 Unknown Site                          24       NA             NA FALSE            TRUE

title: Capacity audits
text: repeated audits, wrap workflow small helper. keeps bulk verification step explicit makes local capacity column configurable. Representative output:
code: add_capacity_audit <- function(data, license_col = license_number, capacity_col = local_capacity) {   data <- data |>     mutate(       .license_input = as.character({{ license_col }}),       .local_capacity = as.integer({{ capacity_col }})     )    verified <- ccld_verify(data$.license_input)    data |>     bind_cols(verified |> select(-input)) |>     mutate(       capacity_delta = capacity - .local_capacity,       capacity_matches = !is.na(capacity) &         !is.na(.local_capacity) &         capacity == .local_capacity,       needs_capacity_review = !found |         is.na(capacity) |         is.na(.local_capacity) |         capacity != .local_capacity     ) |>     select(-.license_input) }  capacity_audit <- add_capacity_audit(sites, license_number, local_capacity) #> # A tibble: 3 x 5 #>   site_name                 capacity local_capacity capacity_delta needs_capacity_review #>   <chr>                        <int>          <int>          <int> <lgl> #> 1 Johnson Family Child Care       14             14              0 FALSE #> 2 Agape Learning Center           60             54              6 TRUE #> 3 Unknown Site                    NA             24             NA TRUE

title: Capacity by geography
text: Start one Alameda snapshot, enrich fields come facility detail endpoint. example uses preschools, pattern works supported ccld_alameda() facility types. Alameda search endpoint useful finding records, return capacity date_closed. Calling ccld_verify() facility numbers fills fields FacilityDetail. Representative output:
code: library(ccldr) library(dplyr) library(ggplot2)  preschools <- ccld_alameda("preschools")  verified <- ccld_verify(preschools$facility_number) |>   select(     facility_number,     verified_found = found,     verified_status = status,     verified_city = city,     capacity,     date_closed,     license_effective_date,     last_visit_date   )  preschools_detail <- preschools |>   select(-capacity, -date_closed, -license_effective_date, -last_visit_date) |>   left_join(verified, by = "facility_number") |>   mutate(     found = coalesce(verified_found, found),     status = coalesce(verified_status, status),     city = coalesce(city, verified_city),     is_closed = !is.na(date_closed) |       grepl("^Closed", status, ignore.case = TRUE),     is_open = found & !is_closed & !is.na(capacity)   ) |>   select(-verified_found, -verified_status, -verified_city) #> # A tibble: 3 x 9 #>   facility_number facility_name          city    status   capacity date_closed is_open last_visit_date found #>   <chr>           <chr>                  <chr>   <chr>       <int> <date>      <lgl>   <date>          <lgl> #> 1 013423751       WILD CHILD SCHOOLHOUSE Oakland Licensed       24 NA          TRUE    2024-09-17      TRUE #> 2 013423056       AGAPE LEARNING CENTER  Oakland Licensed       60 NA          TRUE    2024-11-06      TRUE #> 3 013422467       COLIBRI PRESCHOOL      Oakland Licensed       42 NA          TRUE    2025-02-11      TRUE

title: Capacity by geography
text: Treat open facilities current supply. Closed facilities still valuable audits, mixing current capacity totals overstate supply. Representative output: Representative chart: Look total capacity facility count. city can high total many small sites, large sites, . Representative chart:
code: open_preschools <- preschools_geo |>   filter(is_open)  city_capacity <- open_preschools |>   group_by(city) |>   summarise(     facilities = n(),     total_capacity = sum(capacity),     median_capacity = median(capacity),     capacity_per_facility = total_capacity / facilities,     .groups = "drop"   ) |>   arrange(desc(total_capacity))  city_capacity #> # A tibble: 5 x 5 #>   city     facilities total_capacity median_capacity capacity_per_facility #>   <chr>         <int>          <int>           <dbl>                 <dbl> #> 1 Oakland          64           3080              45                  48.1 #> 2 Fremont          38           1930              48                  50.8 #> 3 Hayward          31           1520              44                  49.0 #> 4 Berkeley         22           1190              50                  54.1 #> 5 Alameda          18            965              48                  53.6 ggplot(city_capacity, aes(x = reorder(city, total_capacity), y = total_capacity)) +   geom_col(fill = "#2b8cbe") +   coord_flip() +   labs(     title = "Total licensed preschool capacity by city",     subtitle = "Open facilities only",     x = NULL,     y = "Licensed capacity"   ) +   theme_minimal() ggplot(city_capacity, aes(x = facilities, y = total_capacity)) +   geom_point(aes(size = median_capacity), alpha = 0.7, color = "#225ea8") +   geom_text(aes(label = city), check_overlap = TRUE, nudge_y = 25, size = 3) +   scale_size_continuous(name = "Median capacity") +   labs(     title = "Facility count and licensed capacity move together, but not perfectly",     x = "Open facilities",     y = "Total licensed capacity"   ) +   theme_minimal()

title: Capacity by geography
text: Use date_closed keep closed records current-supply charts summarize recently closed capacity separate audit. Treat closed capacity facility’s recorded licensed capacity, confirmed seat-loss measure particular program year. Representative output: Representative chart:
code: closed_capacity <- preschools_geo |>   filter(is_closed, !is.na(date_closed)) |>   mutate(closed_year = as.integer(format(date_closed, "%Y"))) |>   group_by(city, closed_year) |>   summarise(     closed_facilities = n(),     closed_capacity = sum(capacity, na.rm = TRUE),     .groups = "drop"   ) |>   arrange(desc(closed_year), desc(closed_capacity))  closed_capacity #> # A tibble: 6 x 4 #>   city     closed_year closed_facilities closed_capacity #>   <chr>          <int>             <int>           <int> #> 1 Oakland         2026                 3             120 #> 2 Fremont         2026                 2              90 #> 3 Hayward         2025                 2              72 #> 4 Berkeley        2025                 1              45 #> 5 Oakland         2024                 2              64 #> 6 Alameda         2024                 1              36 ggplot(closed_capacity, aes(x = closed_year, y = closed_capacity, group = city)) +   geom_line(color = "#636363") +   geom_point(color = "#de2d26") +   facet_wrap(vars(city)) +   labs(     title = "Closed capacity records by city and year",     x = "Closure year",     y = "Recorded capacity on closed facilities"   ) +   theme_minimal()

title: Get started with ccldr
text: Use ccld_verify() vector data-frame column possible license numbers. CCLD API expects facility numbers 9-digit form, ccld_verify() accepts 8- 9-digit inputs pads internally making requests. returns one row per input, including unknown licenses. Example output: Keeping found = FALSE rows result makes audits easier: original records stay visible instead disappearing join.
code: library(ccldr) library(dplyr) library(readr)  rr <- read_csv("rr_sites.csv")  verified <- ccld_verify(rr$license_number)  rr |>   left_join(verified, by = c("license_number" = "input")) |>   select(site_name, license_number, found, facility_name, status, capacity) #> # A tibble: 2 x 6 #>   site_name                 license_number found facility_name       status   capacity #>   <chr>                     <chr>          <lgl> <chr>               <chr>       <int> #> 1 Johnson Family Child Care 13423996       TRUE  JOHNSON III, JOHNNY Licensed       14 #> 2 Unknown Site              99999999       FALSE <NA>                <NA>          NA

title: Get started with ccldr
text: ccld_verify() bulk-friendly path. always returns slim verification schema, one row per input license columns: Example output: full-detail mode inside ccld_verify(). Use screen audit many licenses, call ccld_facilities() need full API detail entire column. ccld_facilities() still calls CCLD one unique license time behind scenes, preserves input rows, duplicate licenses, unknown licenses. Example output:
code: verified |>   names() #>  [1] "input"                  "facility_number" #>  [3] "found"                  "facility_name" #>  [5] "facility_type"          "status" #>  [7] "licensee_name"          "capacity" #>  [9] "street_address"         "city" #> [11] "zip"                    "license_effective_date" #> [13] "date_closed"            "last_visit_date" full <- ccld_facilities(rr$license_number)  full |>   select(input, found, facility_name, visits_total, complaint_count) #> # A tibble: 2 x 5 #>   input    found facility_name       visits_total complaint_count #>   <chr>    <lgl> <chr>                      <int>           <int> #> 1 13423996 TRUE  JOHNSON III, JOHNNY            4               0 #> 2 99999999 FALSE <NA>                          NA              NA

title: Get started with ccldr
text: Use ccld_facility() need full API record one known license. Like ccld_verify(), accepts either 8- 9-digit license form. result one-row tibble scalar facility fields nested list-columns reports complaints. Example output: Example output: Example output: ccld_facility() scalar design. column candidate licenses, run ccld_verify() first. slim output includes capacity date_closed bulk audits, can request full detail facilities need visits, complaint counts, reports, itemized complaints.
code: facility <- ccld_facility("13423996")  facility |>   select(facility_name, status, capacity, last_visit_date) #> # A tibble: 1 x 4 #>   facility_name       status   capacity last_visit_date #>   <chr>               <chr>       <int> <date> #> 1 JOHNSON III, JOHNNY Licensed       14 2024-11-04 facility |>   tidyr::unnest(reports) |>   select(facility_number, report_date, report_type) #> # A tibble: 1 x 3 #>   facility_number report_date report_type #>   <chr>           <date>      <chr> #> 1 013423996       2024-11-04  Other facility |>   tidyr::unnest(complaints) #> # A tibble: 0 x 4 #> # i 4 variables: facility_number <chr>, complaint_date <date>, #> #   allegation <chr>, outcome <chr>

title: Get started with ccldr
text: Every API response cached disk 24 hours default. ccld_cache_info() returns tibble cache file paths, ages, sizes. ccld_cache_clear() returns number cached files removed. fresh response one call, set cache = FALSE: debugging, options useful: Read website articles recurring script patterns troubleshooting: https://chekos.github.io/ccldr/articles/capacity-audits.html https://chekos.github.io/ccldr/articles/capacity-geography-analysis.html https://chekos.github.io/ccldr/articles/closure-date-audits.html https://chekos.github.io/ccldr/articles/live-api-workflows.html https://chekos.github.io/ccldr/articles/troubleshooting.html

what: Why did my license become 9 digits?
title: Troubleshooting and FAQ
text: CCLD’s Transparency API expects facility numbers 9-digit form. Many public local data files store number 8 digits. ccld_pad() adds leading zero requests use API’s canonical form. Representative output:

what: Why does ccld_verify() return found = FALSE?
title: Troubleshooting and FAQ
text: ccld_verify() keeps every input row. API return facility detail license, row stays result found = FALSE missing facility fields. makes failed matches visible joins.

title: Troubleshooting and FAQ
text: License inputs must contain digits must 9 digits fewer. Representative output: Values "ABC123" "0123456789" rejected ccldr_invalid_input error. Representative error:
code: ccld_pad("13423996") ccld_pad(13423996) #> [1] "013423996" #> [1] "013423996" #> Error: #> ! Facility license numbers must contain digits only. #> x Problem value: "ABC123"

title: Troubleshooting and FAQ
text: ccld_alameda() intentionally supports API routes return useful data: "small_fccs" blocked API route used Transparency search. "centers" maps sparse legacy API bucket. small FCC enumeration, use CKAN snapshot chekos/ccld-open-data-snapshot. center workflows, use "preschools".

what: What does the 250-result cap warning mean?
title: Troubleshooting and FAQ
text: CCLD search endpoint can cap individual responses 250 records. reduce risk, ccld_alameda() queries Alameda city separately. city still reports 250 results, function warns additional facilities may hidden API response cap.

what: R Client for the CCLD Transparency API
title: R Client for the CCLD Transparency API
text: ccldr small R client California Community Care Licensing Division (CCLD) Transparency API. Use need : verify CCLD child-care facility license numbers R script; fetch full detail records one facility whole facility table; pull live Alameda County child-care facility snapshot facility type; append Census geographies facility rows addresses. package returns tibbles, keeps unknown licenses output, caches API responses disk repeated development runs gentler upstream service.

title: R Client for the CCLD Transparency API
text: Example output:
code: library(ccldr) library(dplyr) library(readr)  # Verify a column of license numbers without dropping unknown inputs. # ccld_verify() accepts 8- or 9-digit license numbers and pads internally. rr <- read_csv("rr_sites_2026.csv")  verified <- ccld_verify(rr$license_number)  rr |>   left_join(verified, by = c("license_number" = "input")) |>   select(site_name, license_number, found, facility_name, status, capacity) #> # A tibble: 2 x 6 #>   site_name                 license_number found facility_name       status   capacity #>   <chr>                     <chr>          <lgl> <chr>               <chr>       <int> #> 1 Johnson Family Child Care 13423996       TRUE  JOHNSON III, JOHNNY Licensed       14 #> 2 Unknown Site              99999999       FALSE <NA>                <NA>          NA

text: ccld_verify() bulk-friendly path. always returns slim verification schema, one row per input license columns: Example output: full-detail mode inside ccld_verify(). Example output: Pull one full facility record need visits, complaint counts, reports, itemized complaints. ccld_facility() also accepts either 8- 9-digit form: Example output: Example output: ccld_verify() includes capacity date_closed, useful auditing sites bulk. Append Census geography codes need tract, block, ZCTA, school district, geography fields addressable facility rows. Census Geocoder require API key, ccldr caches repeated address lookups. title: R Client for the CCLD Transparency API
text: ccldr talks public APIs. reproducible scripts, keep habits mind: Use cache = FALSE need fresh API response single call. Use ccld_cache_clear() rerunning full workflow scratch. Use options(ccldr.verbose = TRUE) print request paths debugging. Use options(ccldr.delay = 1) slow batch requests. ccld_alameda() walks 17 Alameda cities avoid API’s 250-result response cap. city still hits cap, function warns snapshot may incomplete. ccld_add_census_geographies() calls U.S. Census Geocoder per distinct address, requests layers = "" default, keeps unmatched rows output geocode_status explaining happened.

text: data data frame containing facility address columns. address_col Name street address column. Defaults "street_address". city_col Name city column. title: ccldr 0.3.0
text: Added ccld_facilities() pull full facility detail vector license numbers preserving input rows, duplicate licenses, unknown licenses. Clarified documented split slim bulk-verification output ccld_verify() full single-facility detail ccld_facility(). Expanded workflow articles result-producing examples show representative output, documented future examples must . Added capacity--geography analysis article city, ZCTA, tract, closure-date summaries plus ggplot2 chart examples. Added capacity audit article showing compare local licensed-capacity records ccld_verify() output. ccld_verify() now includes capacity, parsed CCLD CAPACITY field, licensed capacity available bulk verification output. ccld_verify() now includes date_closed, parsed CCLD DATECLOSED field, closure audits can run across vector license numbers. ccld_add_census_geographies() adds -key U.S. Census Geocoder enrichment facility rows, including latitude/longitude, Census tract, block, block group, ZCTA, place, county subdivision, urban area, legislative districts, school district fields available. Census Geocoder responses deduplicated address cached disk, matching package’s existing cache behavior.
